answer.generated: Direct Memory Access (DMA) transfers allow an I/O device to communicate directly with memory, bypassing the CPU. This mechanism is particularly advantageous in scenarios involving large data transfers, such as those encountered in database systems. For instance, when a database server needs to read a substantial amount of data from a disk, a DMA transfer enables the disk controller to send data to main memory without the CPU's intervention, thus freeing the CPU to handle other tasks. This direct communication between the I/O device and memory reduces the load on the CPU and enhances overall system performance. Consider a database system processing a complex query that requires scanning a large dataset stored on disk. During this operation, the database server initiates a DMA transfer to fetch the necessary data blocks into memory. As the DMA controller handles the transfer, the CPU remains available to manage other aspects of the query execution, leading to more efficient use of computational resources.
